description: Objective: one Playwright journey that drives the control room against a REAL daemon - the browser-coverage ledger's daemon-backed lane is UNOWNED and only 3/20 journeys are covered; the two prior tasks for this lane were ARCHIVED (review 2026-08-18 names task-3f503779 - re-measure its scope before reuse, do not blind-re-file). Deliverable: ONE new journey spec that (a) starts a scratch daemon (daemon-main.ts, scratch store, known credential/csrf), (b) seeds one bootstrap chain via the demo seed script (sibling task order 2 - hard dependency, reuse never reimplement), (c) serves the control room in live mode against that daemon (vite dev/preview with MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN, or the serving story the read-only-board task documents), (d) asserts the board renders REAL event-ledger data - the seeded step visible with its truth chips, no fixture markers - and (e) tears down daemon + server with no orphans on Windows. implementationPlan.description: HARNESS PIECE — NEW tests/e2e/control-room/daemon-ports.ts (mirror static-ports.ts's owned-lifecycle style, <=250 lines): owns spawn/readiness/teardown for the journey's three children with the harness's OWN stable reason codes (extend the harness.ts code vocabulary — e.g. E2E_DAEMON_SPAWN_FAILED, E2E_DAEMON_READY_TIMEOUT, E2E_SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT, E2E_TEARDOWN_ORPHAN — exact names measured against harness.ts's existing convention in step 1): (1) spawn REAL `node --experimental-transform-types apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts` with scratch MOE_STORE_PATH, fixed MOE_PROJECT_ID, KNOWN MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL; parse the printed EPHEMERAL origin (never assume 39123); (2) run the REAL seed child (`node apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-main.ts` with its measured env pointed at that origin) and require its success outcome — MOE_SEED_* refusal codes surface verbatim; (3) spawn the control-room dev/preview server child with MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN=<parsed origin>, VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL/VITE_MOE_LIVE_CSRF set to the step-1-measured valid pair, parse ITS bound port; (4) teardown kills all three via taskkill /pid <pid> /t /f semantics treating already-dead as success, then asserts absence via `tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>"`; pids recorded for the journey's origin/pid assertion (DoD 1). No production file edits anywhere in this step.
implementationPlan.note:
Lane lifecycle landed. DEVIATION, disclosed: the plan named ONE new file; a single file measured 314 physical lines, over the 250-line per-file target. Split into three, each with one job: daemon-scratch.ts (145) per-run identities + child env, daemon-children.ts (131) process primitives, daemon-ports.ts (210) the lane composition. No behaviour was dropped to fit.

REASON CODES (this module's own frozen tuple, mirroring harness.ts's convention — harness.ts's four E2E_* codes are the static lane's and are NOT reused): E2E_REPO_ROOT_UNRESOLVED, E2E_DAEMON_SPAWN_FAILED, E2E_DAEMON_READY_TIMEOUT, E2E_SEED_REFUSED, E2E_SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT, E2E_TEARDOWN_ORPHAN. Budgets are per child (daemon 60s, seed 90s, server 60s) so a hang names WHICH child hung, all inside the config's 180s.

(1) DAEMON: real `node --experimental-transform-types apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts --dependencies=<root>/apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts --port=0 --csrf-token=<known>`, env from daemonEnv() — scratch MOE_STORE_PATH, per-run MOE_PROJECT_ID, known MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL, plus the three daemon-side settings the seed cannot supply (MOE_APPROVAL_MODE=SPEED, MOE_SPEED_MODE_DELAY_MS=0 exactly, MOE_NODE_SPECS_DIR). The EPHEMERAL origin is parsed from `^listening on (\S+)$`; 39123 is never assumed.
(2) SEED: the shipped demo-seed-main.ts child, seedEnv() adds MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN (the parsed origin) + MOE_CSRF_TOKEN. Nonzero exit -> E2E_SEED_REFUSED whose detail is the seed's own transcript tail, so a MOE_SEED_* code and its layer surface verbatim rather than restated.
(3) SERVER: `node apps/control-room/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js --port <ephemeral> --strictPort`, cwd apps/control-room, serverEnv() sets MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN plus VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL/VITE_MOE_LIVE_CSRF — or BOTH EMPTY when liveCredentials is "ABSENT", which is how the journey's refusal arm gets a real server with an unconfigured bundle. Readiness parses `Local:\s+(http://localhost:\d+)` and then asserts the announced port EQUALS the requested one, so a second server cannot be driven by mistake.
(4) TEARDOWN: `taskkill /pid <pid> /t /f` per child, newest first (the dev server holds the proxy connection), already-dead treated as success; then absence is CONFIRMED with `tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>" /NH` and any survivor becomes E2E_TEARDOWN_ORPHAN — but only over a SUCCESSFUL primary outcome, never overwriting an earlier reason code. survivingPids() is re-exported so the journey can make the same assertion itself post-run (DoD 3).

Two measured details that would otherwise cost a run each: vite wraps the port DIGITS in SGR escapes (`localhost:ESC[1m62850ESC[22m/`), so output is ANSI-stripped before any pattern sees it; and the spawn-error message is held on an object because a `let` assigned only inside the listener reads as never-assigned at the check.

PER-RUN UNIQUE IDENTITIES (daemon-scratch.ts): nodeRef `node-e2e-<tag>` and projectId `e2e-proj-<tag>` are both derived from the mkdtemp suffix, so the aggregate id the journey asserts on cannot be matched by the committed fixture corpus — that is what makes the positive arm's "this is real daemon data" claim checkable rather than assumed. readWireProtocolVersion() loads GENERATED_WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION from the generated client's committed .js bridge by URL (the same trick vite.config.ts uses for its pins) rather than hand-copying it, since a stale value is answered with DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH at stage COMPATIBILITY.

Verification so far: `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` exit 0 (the lane's own tsc leg, which is the first half of test:e2e:browser). A plain-node smoke of the module is impossible by design — Node's type stripping does not rewrite the `.js` specifiers this directory uses, so the modules are exercised for real in step 3 under Playwright. No production file touched.

implementationPlan.note:
ONE journey, three arms, GREEN against a real daemon: `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts daemon-board` -> exit 0, `1 passed (7.5s)`, `ok 1 [chromium] > daemon-board.spec.ts:155 > the live board renders the daemon's own seeded step, and says so honestly (6.7s)`. Evidence lines the journey printed: `[daemon-lane] daemon pid 33548 at http://127.0.0.1:60681; server pid 17612 at http://localhost:60685; seeded node-e2e-hild2i` and `[daemon-lane] no orphans after teardown: 33548,17612`.

(a) POSITIVE. DoD 1's not-a-static-server proof is four assertions, not a name: the daemon origin matches ^http://127.0.0.1:\d+$, is NOT the served base URL, its pid is nonzero and differs from the server's, and `survivingPids([daemonPid])` confirms the spawned process is ALIVE while the browser is driving it. Then the board: `cr.liveboard.card.node.deliver@<nodeRef>` visible AND present inside `cr.liveboard.column.ready` (a card under the wrong status would still satisfy a bare visibility check) AND containing the nodeRef text. Truth chips: `cr.fact.live.checkpoint` visible with its `cr.chip.observed` carrying data-truth-class=OBSERVED, plus the same chip on `cr.fact.live.connection`.

Why the checkpoint is the load-bearing ledger datum rather than the event list: the SEED consumes and ACKs every page as subscriber `control-room-1` (the only reader the daemon registers), so the browser's timeline is legitimately empty and asserting rows there would be asserting a race. The checkpoint is real ledger state and is stable.

LEDGER-TRUTH CROSS-CHECK. The journey asks the DAEMON the same two questions through the same proxy with the same credentials plus x-moe-protocol-version read from the generated client's committed bridge (a stale value is answered DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH at stage COMPATIBILITY, measured). /affordances/read must answer EXACTLY [{aggregateId: <nodeRef>, kind: "node.deliver", status: "READY"}] for the seeded ref, and /events/read must answer outcome PAGE with a checkpoint whose string the DOM renders character for character (`cr.fact.live.checkpoint` > `cr.value` toHaveText). A static file server can answer neither request.

NOT-A-FIXTURE-COINCIDENCE: nodeRef and projectId are minted per run from the scratch mkdtemp suffix (`node-e2e-hild2i` this run), so the asserted id cannot exist in the committed fixture corpus.

(b) NEGATIVE (DoD 2). The same served bundle re-opened at `?fixtures=1`: `cr.banner.fixture` must be VISIBLE and contain "Fixture board —", and `cr.liveboard` must be absent. This is what makes the positive arm's absence assertion load-bearing — an absence check over a marker that never renders would pass over nothing.

(c) REFUSAL. A second lane with VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL/CSRF both EMPTY: `cr.config.notice` visible containing the literal LIVE_CONFIG_MISSING plus both variable names, and NEITHER `cr.liveboard` NOR `cr.banner.fixture` — no silent fallback in either direction. Note the measured routing: an empty credential pair resolves to CONFIG_NOTICE via shell-mode.ts, not to LiveRefusedPanel, so the code is asserted where it actually renders.

Lane outcome is pinned too (`live.ok ? "ok" : "<code>: <detail>"` compared to "ok"), so a run that refused before the body reports the harness's own reason code instead of reading as a pass, and `survivingPids` is re-asserted by the journey after each lane returns (DoD 3).

Hand-transcribed constants (FIXTURES_QUERY, FIXTURE_MARKER, CREDENTIALS_ABSENT_CODE) follow journeys.spec.ts's rule: this tsconfig cannot reach apps/control-room (TS6059), and deriving them from the rendering module would make the assertions self-referential.
